title: G-O Hike: Orewa Boardwalk
location: 100 Wellington St, Freemans Bay, Auckland
description:
Hello fellow Get‑Outsiders!

Come join us for a peaceful and refreshing walk around the beautiful Ōrewa Estuary. After introductions, we will follow the Te Ara Tahuna shared path, enjoying the calm water, birdlife, boardwalks, and open green spaces. This is a gentle, scenic outing designed to help us slow down, breathe, and enjoy the natural rhythms of the morning.

We will walk the full estuary loop at a relaxed pace, taking time to appreciate the views and the changing landscape as we circle around the water. After completing the loop, we will finish with a short stroll along Ōrewa Beach together before wrapping up (with possible ice cream).

## **IMPORTANT NOTES & UPDATES:**

• **Car‑pool Meeting Point:** 9.00am at **Nishiki Restaurant, Freemans Bay** (meet in the main carpark area). • **Ōrewa Meeting Point:** 10:00am at the **Ōrewa Surf Lifesaving Club carpark** (on the beachfront). • **Official Route Map:** Auckland Council’s Te Ara Tahuna Estuary Pathway map — `https://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/parks-recreation/get-outdoors/Pages/park-details.aspx?Location=Orewa%20Estuary%20Path` (aucklandcouncil.govt.nz in Bing)

• **Difficulty Rating:** Easy (flat shared path, suitable for most fitness levels). • **Suitability:** Ideal for beginners, returning walkers, and anyone wanting a gentle, scenic outing. • **Completion Time:** We expect to finish by around **2:00pm**. • **Footwear:** Comfortable walking shoes; the path is mostly paved or boardwalk. • **Drinking Water:** Please bring your own. • **Toilets:** Public toilets available near the surf club and along the estuary.

• **RSVP to this event:** Please RSVP “Yes” only if you genuinely intend to come. If your plans change, update your RSVP as soon as possible so others can join. Late cancellations (within 24 hours) or no‑shows may be recorded as such. • **Cellphone Coverage:** Good coverage throughout the walk. • **Transport/Car Pooling:** Please answer the car‑pool question when you RSVP to help with planning.

title: Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well-Architected Meetup for 2026!
location: Level 13, Commercial Bay, 15 Customs Street West, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
Hi Architects,

Welcome to the next [AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group](https://www.meetup.com/aws-canberra-well-architected-user-group/) Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

* **Yadwinder Sharma, Founder, https://www.nimbal.ai**

**From 5 Days to 5 Minutes: Reimagining Well-Architected QA with Autonomous AI**

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more

* **Mystery Speaker**

**Well-Architected Agents**
In this talk we will go into the detail of not only the launch of the first Well-Architected agents from both AWS and other AWS partners (and what they can and can't do) but will also go through best-practice agentic architecture as verified by AWS senior architects.

character development
dialogue
structure
setting
point of view
editing
practical tools to strengthen and refine your writing.

As organisations rapidly adopt AI, many struggle to move beyond isolated proofs of concept into secure, scalable, and governed production environments. This session explores how AI Landing Zones provide the foundational platform needed to operationalise AI safely and sustainably at enterprise scale.

He specialises in Azure Landing Zones, cloud governance, and operating model design, working closely with architects, security teams, and business stakeholders to enable secure, scalable cloud and AI adoption. Chanaka has led and advised on complex transformation initiatives across regulated and high‑consumption environments, bridging strategy and hands‑on implementation.

title: Run Better AI Coding Agents for $0 — Straight From Your Own Laptop
location: 36 Lorne Street, Auckland Central ,, Auckland
description:

title: Level Up; Game Design is Business Design with Francis Jones
location: AUT University, Governor Fitzroy Place, Auckland
description:
This month's Level Up will be broken up into two sections; a talk by **Francis Jones** and an **optional playtesting session.** This event will be hosted at AUT with the talk in WG126 and playtesting in the open space outside of that room.

**Game Design is Business Design: Learning from Warrior Chef**
A brutally honest breakdown of why our studio cancelled our game Warrior Chef, diving into how game design decisions shape business strategy and market viability. Francis will cover some fundamental knowledge they've gained over their career, useful for any game designers and current or future indie developers.

**About Francis Jones**
Francis is Co-Founder and Game Director at Rare Parrot Games, with 5 years experience specialising in indie game design and development. Rare Parrot Games is a 3-person studio based in Auckland, and was the winner of the Kiwi Game Starter award at NZGDC in 2022.

**Progress Bar**
Bring down your WIP, demos, or your released titles to show off and receive some feedback. Beyond playing games (or getting feedback on your own) Progress Bar is a great platform for networking, knowledge sharing, celebrating, and socializing!

*NOTE: You are required to bring in your own hardware (laptops, controllers, headphones, etc). If you have specific hardware or space requirements please get in touch to make sure we can accommodate those.*

title: The Queen's Nanny
location: The PumpHouse Theatre, Killarney Park, 2a Manurere Avenue, Takapuna, Auckland 0622, Auckland
description:
Marion Crawford, affectionately known as “Crawfie”, spent sixteen years as nanny to the young princesses Elizabeth and Margaret.
Melanie Tait has constructed a superbly written, witty, insightful and poignant play examining the power, sacrifice, hurt and betrayal of a time in history when loyalty was demanded, the barriers of class were strictly defined, and the right to tell one’s own story was non-existent.
Director Simon Prast steers this personal drama, a commentary on class and the monarchy, into an unmissable night of theatre, with an exceptional cast.
Anna Jullienne plays Crawfie, balancing humour and heartbreak as her loyalty is questioned.
Laura Hill is the Queen Mother, expertly defining the machinations of the House of Windsor, both funny and at times faintly ridiculous.
The third cast member is Jack Buchanan, who has the task of portraying seven characters throughout the play, led by the narrator, steering the action almost as a ringmaster. He also manages to become a butler, an American editor, Crawfie’s fiancée and even a young Elizabeth!
Needless to say, another Tadpole masterpiece not to be missed.
Runtime: Approx. 2 hours with an intervalAge Recommendation: All ages

title: I Was There!
location: Central City Library, 44-46 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
I Was There! celebrates one man’s deep love of live music in Tāmaki Makaurau. This exhibition brings together original gig posters and handwritten set lists from shows attended between 1990 and 1995 - a golden era for New Zealand music fans.
Featuring legendary acts such as The 3Ds, Straitjacket Fits, Able Tasmans, Tall Dwarfs and many more. Each piece is paired with a short personal reflection that captures what it felt like to be in the room on the night.
Curated by longtime gig‑goer Paul Rowe, who has attended hundreds of shows over his lifetime, the exhibition reflects a time when NZ live music was thriving - played loud and late in iconic venues, some of which have since disappeared.
Step back into the 1990s, relive the sweat, noise and moments that mattered. Bring your own musical memories along and reconnect with the gigs this May.

title: Stamptown
location: Q Theatre, Rangatira, 305 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
The New Zealand International Comedy Festival presents - Stamptown.
This is not a 'sit nicely and chuckle' comedy show. Stamptown is a raunchy, chaotic, 90-minute spectacle featuring the most exciting alternative performance from around the world. 
Hosted by bad boy of clown, Zach Zucker, Stamptown is a five-time New York Times Top Comedy Pick (2021-2025). It has packed out rooms at Netflix Is A Joke, Just For Laughs, Edinburgh Fringe, Glastonbury, SXSW, Lincoln Center, Soho Theatre, MICF and Off-Broadway - basically, anywhere people like their comedy sweaty, surprising, and slightly unhinged.
You’re not just watching a show, you’re getting swept up in it. Think big laughs, big swings and the kind of show you have to bring friends to.
“The past, present and future of live entertainment rolled into one magnificently anarchic package.” - Chortle
"An absolutely insane night of comedy that is impossible to replicate, which is what makes it such an appealing show to come back to.” - Broadway World
"Winningly helter-skelter late-night entertainment." - Guardian
"An atmosphere of barely controlled chaos... this is the late night cabaret to see." - Telegraph
“Run for your life if anyone suggests going to see this irredeemably unfunny show.” - Dick Bath, Scottish Field
Recommended 16+.
